Statement on Flood Response and the Urgent Need for Systemic Reform

By Dr Tony Leachon

We commend Mayor Isko Moreno and the  OIC-City Health Officer Dra. Grace Padilla for their swift, proactive response to the recent flooding and public health threats. Their efforts reflect a genuine concern for the welfare of our communities. But let us be clear: temporary relief is not enough.

We cannot normalize a cycle of floods, leptospirosis outbreaks, overwhelmed hospitals, suspended classes, shuttered businesses, and preventable deaths. 

These are not natural disasters—they are symptoms of a deeper affliction: KLEPTOPIROSIS. This is the toxic convergence of corruption, incompetence, and institutional decay that has plagued our flood control systems and public health infrastructure for decades.

📉 The Data Behind the Crisis

• 💸 ₱545.64 billion spent on 9,855 flood control projects from July 2022 to May 2025—yet many flood-prone areas remain submerged 

• 🏗️ P100 billion worth of projects awarded to just 15 contractors, with 6,021 projects lacking clear specifications 

• 🦠 2,396 leptospirosis cases recorded nationwide from June 8 to August 7, 2025, with Metro Manila as the epicenter 

• 🏥 PGH emergency room reached 400% overcapacity, forcing diversion of patients to 20 other hospitals 

• 🏫 Over 24,000 schools suspended classes due to flooding; 732 classrooms destroyed, 442 schools converted into evacuation centers 

• 📉 The Philippines stands to lose $124 billion in GDP by 2050 due to storms, floods, and droughts—$42 billion from floods alone 

The billions poured into the LGU - funded flood control program have yielded little more than submerged streets and broken promises. 

If President Marcos is serious about reform, he must confront this rot head-on—by dismantling the networks of elite capture, enforcing transparency, and holding accountable those who profit from public misery.

We call for a permanent, people-centered solution:

• No floods.
• No leptospirosis.
• No full hospitals.
• No deaths.
• No businesses closed.
• No class suspensions.

This is not just about drainage—it’s about dignity. It’s about restoring trust in our local government units and building institutions that serve, protect, and empower. 

The fight against KLEPTOPIROSIS is the fight for a future where public service is sacred, and every Filipino can walk through their city without fear of disease, displacement, or neglect.

Let this crisis be the turning point. Not just for cleanup—but for clean governance.

#HealthWithHonor 
#MahiyaNamanKayo 
#RelentlessForChange 
#KleptopirosisIsReal

NEWS UPDATE: All U.P. Workers Union-Manila/PGH, along with the All U.P. Academic Employees Union-Manila and UP Manila University Student Council, has issued a unity statement, expressing dismay over the Philippine General Hospital (PGH) administration’s memorandum on responsible social media usage by hospital employees.

The Memorandum 2025-236 released by the PGH admin restricts employees’ posting and airing of grievances on social media platforms, after workers expressed their concerns on the Compensatory Overtime Credit (COC) and the Coterminous with the Incumbent during the recent typhoons and flooding in Manila, which affected the hospital’s workforce.

"We call on the UP Manila administration to revoke the memorandum, which believe violates fundamental rights and basic freedoms, and sets a dangerous precedent," the statement reads. 

Posing a threat to their freedom to express work-related issues, the workers’ unions and the student council call for the revocation of the memorandum and forwarded their concern to the Committee on Academic Freedom and Human Rights (CAFHR) to encourage the hospital admin to collaborate with the employees and uphold free expression.
